title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context (no. 91, attributed to Lexell): find p,q,r,s such that F = λ(p²+s²)(q²+r²)/[pqrs(p²−s²)(q²−r²)] is a square. Read geometrically, this is λ·H1H2/(A1A2) for the two Pythagorean triangles generated by (p,s) and (q,r), with Hi the hypotenuses and Ai the 'areas' ps(p²−s²), qr(q²−r²). That reading is mine; the page does not say so.

On the previous page Euler sets
- p = ax+by, s = bx−ay, q = cx+dy, r = dx−cy. In Gaussian terms p+is ∝ (a+bi)(x−iy), and similarly for q,r.
- r = s, which forces x = a−c, y = b−d.
- p = cc+dd, which removes p from the denominator.

With d = a, c = b−a this page finishes the reduction. The denominator q(p+s)(p−s)(q+r)(q−r) contains the squares (3a−b)², (b−a)², a², (2b−a)². The problem therefore reduces to the single quartic condition λ(a²+b²)(2a−b)(3b−4a) = □, i.e. a genus-1 curve for each λ.

Note. With d = −a one gets c = −a−b, and then
- p = (a+b)²+a², q = −(3a+b)(a+b), r = s = −(a²−ab−b²);
- p±s and q±r factor linearly.
The condition is −λ(a²+b²)(2a+b)(4a+3b) = □. This is the previous one under b → −b. Euler remarks on the unexpected cancellation of four pairs of linear factors.

General solution of the third condition. Euler rewrites cc+dd = aa−ac+bb−bd as (2c+a)²−5a² = (2b−d)²−5d². Hence (2c+a−2b+d)(2c+a+2b−d) = 5(a+d)(a−d), which he parametrizes by mntu:
- a = (mu+nt)/2, d = (mu−nt)/2;
- c = ((5m−n)t+(n−m)u)/4, b = ((5m−n)t−(n−m)u)/4.

The point is that m,n survive only in the scalar C = (5m²−2mn+n²)/16:
- p = C(5t²−2tu+u²), q = −C(t−u)(5t−u), r = s = C(u²−5t²), a²+b² = C(5t²+2tu+u²).
I verified this symbolically and on the cases m=n=1 and m=1, n=0.

After cancelling squares the condition is ±λ(5t²+2tu+u²)(3t−u)(5t−3u) = □. Euler then substitutes u = ν−t and 2t = w, obtaining λ(w²+ν²)(2w−ν)(4w−3ν) = □, with p = w²+(w−ν)², q ∝ (w−ν)(3w−ν), r = s = ν²−νw−w². This is the first solution again with a = w, b = ν. Euler concludes that the 'special' choice d = a was in fact fully general under the conditions r = s, p = c²+d².

Modern explanation, which Euler does not give: (a+bi, c+di, x+iy) → z(a+bi), z(c+di), z(x+iy) only rescales p,q,r,s by |z|². So (p:q:s) depends only on the complex ratio (a+bi):(c+di), which is 2 real parameters. The homogeneous condition p = c²+d² cuts this to a 1-parameter family. That is why the 2-parameter (m,n,t,u) solution collapses to the 1-parameter one.
errors: In the Nota, 'q + r = −a(4a+b)' should be −a(4a+3b). The printed denominator and the final condition correctly use (4a+3b).
In the t,u computation the printed q+r = −2Cu(3t−u), q−r = 2Ct(5t−3u) are wrong. Correctly q+r = −2Ct(5t−3u) and q−r = 2Cu(3t−u). The product (q+r)(q−r) is unaffected, so the conclusion survives.

Sign slip: q = −C(t−u)(5t−u), but the minus is dropped in the displayed denominator. The condition should read −λ(5tt+2tu+uu)(3t−u)(5t−3u) = □, hence −λ(ww+νν)(2w−ν)(4w−3ν) = □. Only with this sign does it coincide, as claimed, with the earlier λ(aa+bb)(2a−b)(3b−4a) = □ for a = w, b = ν. Correspondingly q = −(w−ν)(3w−ν), not +(w−ν)(3w−ν).
Minor: relative to the first solution, s (= r) appears with opposite sign. This is harmless, since rs = s² and p²±s² are invariant.
The parametrization involves divisions by 2 and 4, so integrality is not addressed. This is irrelevant for a homogeneous rational problem.

ideas.what: Writing p²+s² and q²+r² as products of sums of two squares (Brahmagupta–Fibonacci/Gaussian factorization) to clear the numerator, then imposing r = s and p = c²+d² to cancel factors
ideas.modern_name: Gaussian-integer parametrization of sums of two squares; reduction of a Diophantine condition to a quartic y² = λ·(quartic)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Diophantus/Brahmagupta/Fibonacci identity; Euler as systematic user
ideas.where_published: Standard throughout Euler's Diophantine papers and the Algebra (E387/388); this specific problem is unsure

ideas.what: Parametrizing the quaternary quadric (2c+a)²−5a² = (2b−d)²−5d² by factoring a difference of squares with four auxiliary parameters m,n,t,u
ideas.modern_name: Rational parametrization of a quadric via factorization (difference of squares)
ideas.where_published: Common method in Euler's Algebra, part II

ideas.what: Observation that the extra parameters m,n enter only as an overall scale, so the special choice d = a was already the general solution; the 'unexpected' disappearance of four pairs of linear factors
ideas.modern_name: Redundancy of parameters from the Gaussian-unit/scaling symmetry (a+bi, c+di, x+iy) → z·(...); dimension count of the solution family
ideas.usually_credited_to: No specific credit; implicit in later theory of Gaussian integers
ideas.where_published: Only in this posthumous fragment as far as I know

missed.claim: Euler finds, but does not explain, that his 2-parameter general solution of p = c²+d² collapses to the 1-parameter special one. The explanation is the complex-scaling symmetry of the Gaussian factorization p+is ∝ (a+bi)(x−iy). This is a small structural observation, not a new result.
missed.quote: Quae solutio cum praecedente prorsus congruit, ex quo patet illam solutionem multo esse generaliorem, quam initio videbatur.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only: an early instance of noticing parameter redundancy in Diophantine parametrizations. It has no new mathematical content today.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine 18th-century Diophantine manipulation reducing a problem (from Lexell) to a quartic y² = λ·(quartic). Euler's remark that the special solution is general is mildly interesting but elementary. There are minor sign and typo errors. Nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The struck-through line in the print reads 'cc + dd = aa − ac + bb − bd, erit cc + ac − aa = bb − bd − dd, sive'. There is no leading minus before cc; the bracket/minus in the transcription is an artifact of the strike-through.
'q + r = −a(4a+b)' is faithfully transcribed but is a printing error for −a(4a+3b).
In the final substitution the print uses Greek ν (nu) and w, e.g. 'λ(4tt+νν)(4t−ν)(8t−3ν)'; the transcription is correct.
The last displayed denominator in the print is '(t−u)(5t−u) . −2u(t−u)2t(5t−u) . −2u(3t−u)2t(5t−3u)', matching the transcription.
